hints: Start from what a volt means in electricity: $V = W/Q$ with energy $W$ in joules and charge $Q$ in coulombs.
Rewrite those two derived units in SI base units: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$ and $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Divide the base-unit form of the joule by the base-unit form of the coulomb and collect the powers of $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$ to compare with options A to D.
walkthrough: Recall the defining relation for potential difference: $V = W/Q$, so $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$.
Express the joule in base units from work $W = Fs$: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Express the coulomb in base units from charge $Q = It$: $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Substitute into the volt expression: $1 \text{ V} = (1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2})/(1 \text{ A s})$.
Combine powers: dividing by $\text{s}$ gives $\text{s}^{-2-1} = \text{s}^{-3}$ and dividing by $\text{A}$ gives $\text{A}^{-1}$, so $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}$.

options.A: Gives $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-1}\text{A}^{-1}$ which has $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$, so it is too large by $\text{s}^{2}$ and cannot equal $W/Q$.
options.B: Gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2}\text{A}$ which is newton times ampere, with $\text{A}^{+1}$ instead of $\text{A}^{-1}$ and missing one power of $\text{m}$ and one of $\text{s}^{-1}$.
options.C: Gives $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-1}\text{A}$ which has both $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$ powers wrong for energy divided by charge.
options.D: Gives $\text{kg m}^{2}\text{s}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}$ which matches $\text{J C}^{-1}$ expressed in $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$.
